body.statement:
Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied, and fix a successful finite output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). There are events \(\mathcal H_m\) with \(\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}(\mathcal H_m)\to1\) such that, on \(\mathcal H_m\), \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}\) is nonempty and is bijectively matched to \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\). With the empty-set convention in \(d_H\), uniformly over \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\), \(d_H(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m},\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma))=O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})\) and \(\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing)\to0\). Under local branch labels,
\[
\sqrt m\{r(\pi_G(S_m))-r(\Sigma)\}\rightsquigarrow N\!\left(0,Dr(\Sigma)D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}Dr(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}\right).
\]
The simultaneous neighborhoods \(\mathcal A_m\) cover every retained branch with asymptotic probability at least \(1-\alpha\), uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\).
body.proof_tex:
Let \(q=n(n+1)/2\), fix an ordering \(\operatorname{vech}\) of symmetric entries, and set
\[
 W_r=\operatorname{vech}\!\left(
 X^{(r)}X^{(r)\mathsf T}-\Sigma\right).
\]
Then
\[
 \sqrt m\,\operatorname{vech}(S_m-\Sigma)
 =m^{-1/2}\sum_{r=1}^mW_r.
\tag{53}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}gaussian}\), the summands are independent and centered.  Differentiating the Gaussian moment-generating function gives
\[
 \mathbb E(X_iX_jX_kX_l)
 =\sigma_{ij}\sigma_{kl}+\sigma_{ik}\sigma_{jl}
  +\sigma_{il}\sigma_{jk},
\]
and consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(W_{r,ij},W_{r,kl})
 =\sigma_{ik}\sigma_{jl}+\sigma_{il}\sigma_{jk}
 =(V_\Sigma)_{ij,kl}.
\tag{54}
\]

Compactness of \(\mathcal K_G\) uniformly bounds all fixed Gaussian moments, including \(\mathbb E_\Sigma\|W_r\|^3\).  Taylor expansion of \(e^{ix}\) therefore gives, for fixed \(u\in\mathbb R^q\), uniformly in \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\),
\[
 \mathbb E_\Sigma\exp\!\left(
 \frac{iu^{\mathsf T}W_r}{\sqrt m}\right)
 =1-\frac{u^{\mathsf T}V_\Sigma u}{2m}+O(m^{-3/2}).
\tag{55}
\]
Taking the \(m\)-th power proves the covariance central limit law.  Uniformity follows by the subsequence principle: every sequence \(\Sigma_m\in\mathcal K_G\) has a convergent subsequence, (55) identifies every weak subsequential limit, and the uniformly bounded second moments give tightness.  Hence
\[
 \sqrt m\,\operatorname{vech}(S_m-\Sigma)
 \rightsquigarrow N(0,V_\Sigma)
\tag{56}
\]
uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\), and Chebyshev's inequality gives
\[
 \|S_m-\Sigma\|=O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})
\tag{57}
\]
uniformly.

Write \(\widehat\Sigma_m=\pi_G(S_m)\) on the projection tube.  Because \(\pi_G(\Sigma)=\Sigma\) on the smooth stratum, smoothness and compactness give the uniform Taylor expansion
\[
 \operatorname{vech}(\widehat\Sigma_m-\Sigma)
 =D\pi_G(\Sigma)\operatorname{vech}(S_m-\Sigma)
  +O_{\mathbb P}(\|S_m-\Sigma\|^2).
\tag{58}
\]
Every coefficient circuit of \(p_e\) is smooth near \(\mathcal K_G\), since its denominators are bounded away from zero.  The derived separation lemma supplies a common separation margin and a positive lower bound for \(|\partial_tp_e|\) at every root.  The implicit-function calculation therefore produces one unique smooth branch through every retained root, with uniformly bounded first and second derivatives on a finite cover of \(\mathcal K_G\), and
\[
 Dr_j(\Sigma)[H]
 =-\frac{D_\Sigma p_e(\Sigma,r_j(\Sigma))[H]}
         {\partial_tp_e(\Sigma,r_j(\Sigma))}.
\tag{59}
\]
Increasing order, separation, and constancy of the extension labels on the connected regular cell give the common labeling \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_J)\).  Combining (56)--(59) gives, uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\),
\[
 \sqrt m\{r(\pi_G(S_m))-r(\Sigma)\}
 \rightsquigarrow N\!\left(0,
 Dr(\Sigma)D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma
 D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}Dr(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}
 \right).
\tag{60}
\]

Every certificate factor is continuous and nonzero on \(\mathcal K_G\), and all extension labels are locally constant on the selected cell.  Compactness therefore supplies a relative neighborhood \(U\) on which the projection is defined, every certificate stays valid, and the same \(J\) branches are retained.  Let \(\gamma\) be the derived separation margin and define
\[
 \mathcal H_m=\left\{
 \begin{array}{l}
 S_m\text{ lies in the projection tube},\quad
 \widehat\Sigma_m\in U,\\[2pt]
 \displaystyle\max_{1\le j\le J}
 |r_j(\widehat\Sigma_m)-r_j(\Sigma)|<\gamma/3
 \end{array}\right\}.
\tag{61}
\]
Uniform consistency in (57)--(58), uniform continuity of the roots, and the positive certificate margins imply
\[
 \inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_\Sigma(\mathcal H_m)\to1.
\tag{62}
\]
On \(\mathcal H_m\), the real-lifting theorem and \(\mathrm{def:finite\mbox{-}set\mbox{-}estimator}\) give
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}
 =\{r_1(\widehat\Sigma_m),\ldots,r_J(\widehat\Sigma_m)\}.
\tag{63}
\]
The separation in (61) makes (63) a bijective matching to \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\).  The regular-cell lemma gives \(J\ge1\), so it is nonempty.  Moreover,
\[
 d_H\!\left(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m},
             \mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\right)
 \le\max_j|r_j(\widehat\Sigma_m)-r_j(\Sigma)|
 =O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})
\tag{64}
\]
uniformly.  Although the stipulated Hausdorff distance can be infinite on \(\mathcal H_m^c\), (62) makes that event uniformly negligible, which is exactly the definition of the uniform \(O_{\mathbb P}\) claim.  Also
\[
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}
 \Pr_\Sigma(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing)
 \le\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_\Sigma(\mathcal H_m^c)
 \to0.
\tag{65}
\]

For simultaneous neighborhoods, let \(s=\dim\mathcal C_{G,e}\) and
\[
 W_\pi(\Sigma)=D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
For a nonzero symmetric direction \(H\), the Gaussian fourth-moment identity gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_\Sigma(X^{\mathsf T}HX)
 =2\operatorname{tr}\!\left((\Sigma^{1/2}H\Sigma^{1/2})^2\right)>0.
\tag{66}
\]
Thus \(V_\Sigma\) is positive definite on symmetric-coordinate directions.  Since the nearest-point projection fixes the stratum, \(D\pi_G\) is the identity on its tangent space and has that \(s\)-dimensional space as image.  Hence \(W_\pi\) has constant rank \(s\); compactness bounds its smallest positive eigenvalue away from zero, so its Moore--Penrose inverse is continuous.  With the plug-in matrix \(\widehat W_{\pi,m}\), equations (56)--(58) and continuous mapping give
\[
 m\,\operatorname{vech}(\widehat\Sigma_m-\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}
 \widehat W_{\pi,m}^{+}
 \operatorname{vech}(\widehat\Sigma_m-\Sigma)
 \rightsquigarrow\chi_s^2
\tag{67}
\]
uniformly.  Indeed, if \(Z\sim N(0,W_\pi)\), then \(Z^{\mathsf T}W_\pi^+Z\) is a sum of \(s\) independent squared standard normals.

Let \(E_m\) be the corresponding confidence ellipsoid centered at \(\widehat\Sigma_m\), intersected with the regular projected neighborhood, using the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(\chi_s^2\).  Equation (67) yields
\[
 \liminf_{m\to\infty}\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}
 \Pr_\Sigma(\Sigma\in E_m)\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{68}
\]
For \(s=0\), use the degenerate ellipsoid at the locally constant projected point, with limiting coverage one.  As in \(\mathrm{def:branch\mbox{-}neighborhoods}\), set \(\mathcal A_{m,j}=r_j(E_m)\).  Whenever \(\Sigma\in E_m\), all inclusions \(r_j(\Sigma)\in\mathcal A_{m,j}\) hold simultaneously.  Therefore
\[
 \liminf_{m\to\infty}\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}
 \Pr_\Sigma\!\left(
 r_j(\Sigma)\in\mathcal A_{m,j}\text{ for all }1\le j\le J
 \right)\ge1-\alpha.
\]
This covers every retained branch and selects none.
body.justification: The observationally equivalent branches are the estimand, so inference must cover them simultaneously rather than select one.
body.gap: Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer treat general criterion-defined sets, while Mareis, Sturma, and Drton derive regular half-trek point inference; neither gives root-specific joint inference for a finite algebraic SEM coordinate fiber.
body.consumer: Researchers using a graph with added parents can report sampling uncertainty around every compatible direct-effect branch.
